datatype_sweep.clip_bar_note: The brief's bar -- e2e CLIP within 0.02 of the p300x2 bf16 clip at the same prompt/seed -- is NOT met as literally written: p150 bf8 at 1344x768 x124 scores 0.341777 against p300x2 bf16's 0.308699, 0.033 apart. That comparison is not informative at this resolution and the matrix is the evidence: CLIP's own spread between adjacent working points of ONE identical configuration is far larger than the bar (p150 1344x768 NFE4: 0.341777 at 124 frames vs 0.297044 at 73; p300x2 1344x768 NFE4: 0.308699 vs 0.183873). Different meshes sample different trajectories, so a cross-mesh CLIP delta measures the sample, not the fidelity. The dtype question was therefore settled on the SAME mesh at the SAME point (see rejected[]), where the bar does discriminate, plus stage 04's component PCC bars and 16/16 content checks on all 15 clips.
datatype_sweep.content_checks: 15 of 15 clips pass all 16 prove_h3 checks, 0 critical failures; every CLIP score is above the calibrated floor 0.144909 (lowest 0.183873)
not_measured: compute-fidelity sweep (HiFi2 / HiFi4 / LoFi): the tt_dit MiniMax-H3 path takes fidelity from its matmul program configs and exposes no profile knob for it, so this needs a code change and is deferred with the fp32-tail-block work

fp32 tail blocks on/off: bf16_blocks is wired and reachable as bf4_ff_keep_ends, but no accuracy pressure was found that needed it -- the chosen bf8 policy already carries stage 04's component PCC bars

text encoder bf16 vs bfp8 on device: p150 serves the conditioner on HOST (the on-device one dies in decoder layer 30 of 50 on a 32 GB part, stage 03), so there is no on-device dtype to sweep there; on p300x2 it is on device at bf16 and was not swept

p150_policy.profile_note: this block records the STAGE 05 storage sweep, whose winner was bf8_weights_bf8_out. Stage 06 then changed the ARITHMETIC (fp32 destination accumulate off) on the same storage, which is a different profile NAME for the same cached tensorbins, so the served p150.dit_quant_profile is bf8_weights_bf8_out_nofp32acc and this block's `profile` is not the served one. Flagged by the third stage-review as an internal contradiction; it is a provenance-versus-served distinction and it is now labelled rather than silently divergent.
p150_policy.why: the only alternative measured (bf4_ff) is not faster and costs CLIP; see rejected[]

p300x2_policy.why: the (1,4) preset asks for no quant profile; TP=4 divides the DiT to ~16.6 GB/chip and the measured default already clears the 90 s budget at 75.5 s, so there is nothing to buy by quantizing. This block records the stage-05 sweep as it was taken. CORRECTED 2026-10-05 (06b): the stage-06 note that once stood here -- that the served-point quality defect lived on this bf16 path and went away at bf8 -- is withdrawn. The defect was the LoRA bind dying on a weight page-in, and this mesh now serves correct output at bf16. See p300x2.quality.

rejected.controlled_against: bf8_weights_bf8_out, same mesh (p150 1x1), same point 1344x768 x124, same adapter/shift/prompt/seed
rejected.verdict: rejected on both axes: 0.9 s is inside run-to-run noise, so bf4 on ff1/ff2 buys no time, and it costs 0.026 of CLIP -- past the 0.02 bar. It is a MEMORY lever (-5.38 GiB), worth keeping in the registry for a canvas that does not otherwise fit, not a speed lever.

optimized_by: stage 06 (see artifacts/s06/results.json); the matrix[] rows are stage 05 measurements at the PRE-optimization tree and are left as recorded. p150's DEFAULT also changed working point here -- NFE 8 -> NFE 4 on a five-prompt paired tiebreak -- which is a separate thing from the optimization gain and is recorded as such in p150.choice_reason and p150.superseded_nfe8_point. datatype_sweep[] is likewise a stage-05 record: its p150_policy.profile is the storage winner, not the served profile -- see datatype_sweep.p150_policy.profile_note.

p150.choice_reason: NFE 4, on the tiebreak stage 06 finally ran. Stage 05 chose NFE 8 on a +0.0582 CLIP margin at ONE prompt while recording that CLIP's own spread between adjacent points of one identical configuration is ~0.045. Re-run PAIRED over five prompts at this exact point and seed: NFE 8 wins 3 of 5, mean delta +0.0106 with a per-prompt stdev of 0.0255 (sem 0.0114, paired t 0.93 -- not distinguishable from zero), and the entire margin is the one prompt the original decision was made on: excluding it the mean delta is -0.0004. The latency price for that unestablished effect was 38.9%. Counter-reading, stated rather than hidden: stage 05's literal rule was 'keep the higher NFE if the margin is >= 0.01' and the 5-prompt mean margin (+0.0106) technically still clears it -- but that rule reads a mean without its spread, which is the flaw that produced the wrong answer the first time. Reverting is one line and every number is in the stage-06 record (nfe_tiebreak). The 80.6 s here is worst-of-five warm samples measured AT this profile; it is a working-point change and NOT part of stage 06's 147.7 -> 134.2 s optimization gain, which was measured at the NFE 8 point this default has now left.

dit_dtype_policy.mm_fp32_dest_acc_en_scope: all four block matmuls: to_qkv and to_out via attention_kwargs, ff1 and ff2 via the block. The block's config also reaches adaln_proj, a fifth matmul, but precomputed_adaln is true here so that projection never exists on device.
dit_dtype_policy.why: bf4_ff, the only storage alternative measured, is not faster and costs CLIP (see rejected[]). The arithmetic is a separate axis and stage 06 measured it over all four block matmuls: fp32 destination accumulation off is 2.5% of a block and 1.6% of the e2e, with full-depth video PCC 0.9930 against bf8_weights_bf8_out's 0.9927 and audio 0.9799 against 0.9840 (bars 0.99/0.95). LoFi is 12.5% of a block but scores video 0.9892, under the 0.99 bar by 0.0008, and is not offered as a profile; LoFi with bf16_blocks=(0,-1) was tried and is WORSE, video 0.9858, so the escape hatch this class documents does not buy back the 0.0008 and LoFi is rejected at both configurations.

p150.frames_headroom_MEASURED: MEASURED, not extrapolated: 1344x768 x124 at NFE 4 on this served profile is 157.9 / 161.9 s over two prompts (worst 161.9), INSIDE the 180 s budget, 16/16 content checks and 0 critical on both, CLIP 0.3366 / 0.3260 -- for 5.2 s of video instead of 3.0. The earlier ~165 s arithmetic was right. artifacts/s06/controls/ctlB_p150_x124.json. It is still NOT taken as the default here: that is a SECOND working-point knob and stage 06 had already moved one (NFE 8 -> 4), so stage 07/09 owns the decision -- but it now owns a measurement instead of an estimate.

superseded_nfe8_point.why_kept: this is the point stage 06's OPTIMIZATION gain was measured at, and losing it would leave the 147.7 -> 134.2 s pair with nothing in this file to anchor it. It is no longer the default; the tiebreak moved the default to NFE 4.

tiebreak.content_checks: 16/16, 0 critical, on all ten tiebreak clips and all five served-profile clips

p300x2.choice_reason: chosen on latency and canvas; the quality fence this line used to carry is LIFTED -- see `quality`, re-taken 2026-10-05 on the build that fixed the on-device LoRA bind. Within budget. Stage 06 took the e2e from 75.5 s to 71.7 s here: the (1,4) preset has sp_axis 0 over a mesh of shape (1,4), so sp_factor is 1 and the ring-free windowed SDPA path applies on this mesh too -- but with 14 heads per device rather than p150's 56, and the chunk-size optimum moves with head count, so this mesh takes (512, 128) where p150 takes (384, 256). Measured at 14 heads at all three lengths this profile can serve: 19328 -11.8%, 22464 -4.2%, 37760 -4.8% against the 56-head pick. CLIP 0.3344 against stage 05's 0.3087 at the same point; the chunking changes flash attention's reduction order, so this is a different trajectory rather than the same clip measured again, and the delta is inside the point-to-point CLIP spread this file documents under datatype_sweep.clip_bar_note.

dit_dtype_policy.why: the (1,4) preset asks for no quant profile: TP=4 divides the DiT to ~16.6 GB/chip and the measured default clears the 90 s budget, so there is nothing to buy by quantizing on latency. CORRECTED 2026-10-05 (06b): the stage-06 sentence that the served-point quality defect 'lives on this bf16 path' is WITHDRAWN. The defect was the on-device LoRA bind not surviving a weight page-in; it is fixed in the shared layer and this profile's quality is re-taken as good at bf16. bf8 appeared to cure it only because a quant profile also moves the adapter to the host fuse. Nothing about the dtype needs to change.

p300x2.e2e_note: WORST of five prompts on the fixed build (stage 06b), against stage 06's 71.7 s worst-of-two. The difference is the fix's one new per-request cost: re-applying the adapter on the DiT page-in re-uploads 208 rank-128 A/B pairs from host. It is invisible in phases_s -- denoising is unchanged (36.1 s on the coastline prompt against the no-adapter control's 35.9 s, so the merge still has no per-step cost) -- and shows up as wall-minus-phases going 17.6 s -> 20.1 s, flat across all five clips. Peak DRAM is unchanged at 19.94 GiB (lora_cache_capacity is 0, so the factors are freed per apply). Still inside the 90 s budget. Removable: LoRAMixin's A/B LRU exists for exactly this re-merge and would buy the 2.4 s back for about 0.5 GiB/device; not taken in 06b because it moves the memory profile this record was measured at.
p300x2.quality: RE-TAKEN 2026-10-05 (stage 06b) on the fixed build and now GOOD. The stage-06 defect was not a working-point problem at all: the on-device LoRA bind was inert across the DiT page-in this `coresident: False` preset performs before every denoise, so every clip ever recorded on this profile was BASE-model output. Fixed in tt_dit's shared LoRA layer (commit 'Keep a fuse-mode LoRA bound across a weight page-out'). Five prompts, seed 7, one build, warm, at this exact point: CLIP 0.3239 / 0.3589 / 0.3690 / 0.3218 / 0.3381, temporal motion 8.47 / 6.44 / 1.28 / 3.10 / 1.96. The motion collapse is gone (it was a 0.70-0.89 floor on 3 of 5), the content-free coastline clip is gone (CLIP 0.1867 -> 0.3690) and the dark blacksmith clip is back in p150's range (video mean 4.0 -> 11.1 against p150's 13.9). Cross-checked against stage 06's INDEPENDENT bf16 host-fuse control ctlF, a different code path to the same model, on its two prompts: coastline 0.3690/1.28/107.7 here against ctlF's 0.3647/1.239/108.5, blacksmith 0.3218/3.10/11.1 against 0.3227/2.529/10.4. artifacts/s06b/results.json.
p300x2.quality_fix_measured: SUPERSEDED 2026-10-05 by the real fix; kept only so the stage-06 reading is not silently deleted. The one-axis bisect that produced it was sound as measurement and wrong as diagnosis: ctlE's bf8 arm recovered the output because setting a quant profile ALSO switches the adapter onto the host-fuse path (`_lora_fuses_on_host`), not because bf16 arithmetic was the problem. ctlF held the dtype at bf16, forced the host fuse, and recovered everything too -- which already exonerated the dtype inside stage 06. There is no accuracy reason to quantize this mesh. See artifacts/s06b/results.json.
p300x2.quality_known_exception: 1 of the 5 clips fails exactly one critical prove_h3 check and it is NOT this profile's problem: 'a red fox trotting through fresh snow at dawn, crisp footsteps crunching' scores audio rms 0.0019 against prove_h3's absolute 0.002 floor. The SAME prompt and point run through the independent host-fuse path (MINIMAX_H3_FORCE_HOST_FUSE=1) gives 0.0018 and fails the same check, with CLIP 0.3598 against 0.3589 and motion 6.32 against 6.44 -- so the two adapter-application paths agree and the quiet audio is the prompt. It is also the quietest prompt of the five on p150 (rms 0.00500 at 73 frames, the lowest of its five), and this clip is 124 frames / 5.2 s of audio against p150's 73 / 3.0 s, so sparse footsteps spread over a longer clip land lower in RMS. Stage 07 owns the call: either prove_h3's audio floor is made duration-aware, or this prompt is expected to fail it on a 5 s clip. Nothing here says the model is wrong. artifacts/s06b/s06b_ctlH_fox_hostfuse.json.
p300x2.within_budget_note: `within_budget` and `e2e_s` are latency facts and remain true. They say nothing about whether the clip is correct; see `quality`.
